title: Green-biorefinery life-cycle inventory for four grass and fractionation scenarios
publication: Science of the Total Environment, Volume 949, Article 175035
license: CC BY 4.0, as stated on the institutional repository record for the article
source_location: Table 3, pp. 5-6 of the open author manuscript
functional_unit: 1 t dry matter of crude protein delivered from leaf protein concentrate (LPC-CP), as defined in the article methods and Table 3 caption

scenarios.F1TP1: Perennial ryegrass feedstock; Technology Pathway 1, one-stage maceration
scenarios.F1TP2: Perennial ryegrass feedstock; Technology Pathway 2, multi-stage maceration
scenarios.F2TP1: Grass-clover feedstock; Technology Pathway 1, one-stage maceration
scenarios.F2TP2: Grass-clover feedstock; Technology Pathway 2, multi-stage maceration

data_origin_and_scope.demonstration_plant: The article states that primary mass and energy balances, three main co-product yields, and DM/CP concentrations were measured at the Aarhus University demonstration platform using an integrated PLC/data-collection system. The Table 3 scenario results are scaled to the functional unit; raw batch-level records are not included in this transcription.
data_origin_and_scope.feedstock_agriculture: Cultivation inputs, yields, land use, transport, and related emissions are LCA scenario inventory values; feedstock production and fertilizer-related emissions were calculated using cited secondary methods and sources.
data_origin_and_scope.anaerobic_digestion: Brown-juice anaerobic digestion, CHP co-products, digestate substitution, and AD/storage/application emissions were modelled using an adapted LCAD tool, not measured as a continuous GreenHub digestion campaign.
data_origin_and_scope.transport: Study scenario distances are used; article methods state average 10 km for feedstock and digestate/press cake and 50 km for protein transport. These are not GreenHub distances.

data_handling: Direct transcription of the 42 Table 3 flow rows across four baseline scenarios. No recalculation, unit conversion, annualization, graph digitization, or replacement of source values was performed.
sign_convention: Negative CHP energy and digestate nutrient entries are LCI coproduct/substitution credits. They are not negative physical generation, negative nutrient content, or GreenHub recovery yields.
unit_caveats: The table lists biorefinery heat input in kW despite a mass-based functional unit; the time normalization is unclear. The value is retained exactly as published and must not be converted to kWh per tonne without the supplement or author clarification.
Nitrate rows are kg NO3, not kg nitrate-N.
Phosphorus and potassium coproduct rows use P2O5 and K2O bases; they are not elemental P and K.
The press-cake and LPC product moisture basis is not stated in Table 3.
supplementary_data_status: The institutional record lists a 385 kB supplementary Excel workbook. Its public download endpoint returned HTTP 403 in this collection pass, so the workbook was not downloaded. This CSV contains only accessible Table 3 manuscript values, not the unavailable workbook or its additional tables.
limitations: Irish/Danish cultivated ryegrass and grass-clover biorefinery scenarios are not Dutch roadside-grass GreenHub measurements.
Primary pilot data are aggregated/scaled to a protein-based functional unit; treatment-level raw measurements and uncertainty are not included here.
AD, digestate, fertilizer substitution, field emissions and transport results are modelled LCI values with study-specific boundaries and assumptions.
The data do not provide a GreenHub route validation, product credit, emission factor, or parameter default.
The separate supplementary Excel may contain additional details; its inaccessible download remains an open collection task.
